1_executive_email.body:
Dear Implantable device company with immunology expertise Technology Scouting / R&D Leadership,

I am writing to present a technology-transfer opportunity that may be of strategic interest to Implantable device company with immunology expertise.

## Technology
P-20 — Dual anti-fibrotic: CD47-mimetic glycan surface (immune tolerance) + IL-1

## Why This May Matter to Implantable device company with immunology expertise or coating technology company
Foreign-body response limits implant lifetime. Glycan-mediated immune tolerance could extend implant longevity across multiple device categories.

## Current Evidence
- Technical readiness: T1
- Physical validation: NONE
- Evidence is transparent and auditable — every claim traces to a source artifact

## What Is NOT Proven (Honest Disclosure)
- NO_FAILURES_TESTED_YET — all evidence is MODELLED. Buyer should treat all claims as untested hypotheses until decisive experiment is commissioned.

## What We Are Asking
Request technical diligence. Commission additional computational verification OR the decisive experiment. Licensing is a subsequent route after technical maturity is established.

## Validation Investment
A defined experiment ($$10-15K, 12-18 months to T2) can upgrade this from T1 to externally verified status.

## Next Step
If this is of interest, I would welcome a 30-minute call to discuss:
1. Whether this fits your strategic roadmap
2. What evidence you would need to evaluate further
3. Whether a sponsored validation or co-development structure makes sense

I can share the full technical dossier under NDA.

Best regards,
[CEO Name]
CereVascular

2_one_page_opportunity_summary:
# P-20 — Technology Transfer Opportunity

**Technology:** P-20 — Dual anti-fibrotic: CD47-mimetic glycan surface (immune tolerance) + IL-1
**Buyer:** Implantable device company with immunology expertise or coating technology company
**Current Evidence:** T1 | NONE
**Recommended Transaction:** SPONSORED_VALIDATION (IL-10 release in aCSF)
**Validation Cost:** $10-15K (12-18 months to T2)

## Problem
Fibrotic encapsulation = 10-15% of shunt failures. Passive coatings have limited efficacy.

## Technology
P-20 — Dual anti-fibrotic: CD47-mimetic glycan surface (immune tolerance) + IL-10 analo

## Strategic Value
Platform — immune tolerance coating for any implant

## What Is Proven
- Computational model: yes
- External verification: no
- Physical validation: no

## What Is NOT Proven
- NO_FAILURES_TESTED_YET — all evidence is MODELLED. Buyer should treat all claims as untested hypotheses until decisive experiment is commissioned.

## Strongest Alternative
Passive coatings (phosphorylcholine) — no active immune tolerance

## Decisive Question
Actual IL-10 release in CSF. Glycan surface density degradation. In vivo fibrosis reduction.

## What We Are Asking You to Do
Request technical diligence. Commission additional computational verification OR the decisive experiment. Licensing is a subsequent route after technical maturity is established.
